hooks.text: Jupiter was once twice as wide as it is today.
What planet once swallowed the volume of 8,000 Earths?
Jupiter used to be double its current size.

title: Jupiter Was Once Twice Its Current Size
description: Jupiter is the undisputed architect of our solar system, but it used to be much larger. Primordial Jupiter once commanded a volume equivalent to 8,000 Earths.

beats.text: Jupiter was once twice as wide as it is today.
beats.visual: Artist's concept of primordial Jupiter accreting within the early protoplanetary disk

beats.text: That ancient monster could have swallowed 8,000 Earths.
beats.visual: Infographic showing a size comparison between Earth and a giant primordial Jupiter

beats.text: Even now, every other planet fits inside it twice over.
beats.visual: NASA diagram showing all solar system planets tucked inside Jupiter's volume

beats.text: Its gravity was so strong it sculpted our entire solar system.
beats.visual: Animation of Jupiter's gravity affecting the orbits of nearby planetesimals

beats.text: Jupiter rotates so fast a full day lasts ten hours.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope 2024 full rotation sequence of Jupiter's cloud decks

beats.text: This speed feeds a storm bigger than the Earth itself.
beats.visual: Juno spacecraft high-resolution close-up of the Great Red Spot's swirling clouds

beats.text: The volcanic moon Io is being stretched by that massive pull.
beats.visual: New Horizons photograph of the volcanic moon Io against Jupiter's cloud deck, 2007

beats.text: But modern Jupiter is just a remnant of that former self.
beats.visual: Artist concept of a massive early Jupiter compared to the current planet

beats.text: The gas giant was once twice as wide.
beats.visual: Artist's concept of primordial Jupiter accreting within the early protoplanetary disk

better_than_last: Applied the proven rule of using a familiar physical scale comparison (8,000 Earths) in beat 2 to anchor the cosmic-scale hook.
